I will start from what I did before and only adjust a little. On my wheat-maize land, I will keep the stronger ground for grain because that is my steady money, and I will put stevia on the smaller piece because it needs more hand work and more careful watching. I have 16.1 mu total, and with only 2 people in the house, I will not spread myself too thin. I will keep 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu in stevia. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer so the seedlings come up strong, then chase nitrogen again at jointing with one good watering. Around here, if I save too much on wheat fertilizer, I will see it in the ears later, so I would rather spend a bit more and hold yield. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people here do, sow quickly after harvest, keep the rows clean, and feed it mainly around the big bell-mouth stage. I have well irrigation, so if rain is short I will not wait too long. For stevia, I will manage it a bit tighter because it responds to water and fertilizer, but I will still watch cost; too much spending on one crop can squeeze the rest. I will follow what has worked in nearby fields, use a little more when I feel the stand needs protection, and keep the plan steady instead of making big risky changes.
